title: A Novel Technique for Generating and Observing Chemiluminescence in a Biological Setting
protocol: Attach wood part A upright in the center of part B using two screws.
Attach wood part C to the middle of part A using one screw, ensuring that part C can still be moved.
Drill two holes through the lower tip of the spray bottle trigger and push a stainless steel rod through to form two loops on either side of the trigger.
Wrap the bottom part of the spray bottle with duct tape to prevent cable ties from slipping off.
Attach the spray bottle to wood part C using two plastic cable ties.
Cut off the connector of the servo motor and reconnect it with the loose cables of the servo control.
Attach the servo motor to the top of wood part A using duct tape.
Attach a pencil to the servo motor lever using a paper clip.
Tightly connect the outermost parts of the pencil to the steel rod loops with plastic covered twist wires.
Secure the ends on the pencil with duct tape.
Cut off the servo motor control unit's magnetic cable connector and reattach it to the speaker cable.
Tape the servo motor control unit to wood part B (12.7 x 10.7 x 1.8 cm3).
Cut a w1 cable with magnetic connectors in half and attach one part to the loose end of the copper speaker cable.
Connect the (magnetic) i2 toggle switch and p1 power to the available w1 cable.
Attach a 9V battery to complete the setup.

In a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, prepare solutions of [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2 in reverse osmosis water (100 µL) at concentrations of 260 µg, 52 µg, 26 µg, 5 µg, 3 µg, 520 ng, 260 ng, 52 ng, 26 ng, 5 ng, and 3 ng.
Mix 100 µL of each [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2 solution with 100 µL of an aqueous solution of ammonium cerium nitrate ((NH4)2Ce(NO3)6) in water (25 mM).
Set up the acquisition in the bioluminescence reader by initializing the imaging software.
Sign in to the user profile and look for the acquisition control panel.
Click on "Initialize" and wait until the instrument is ready.
Make sure "Luminescent" and "Photograph" are checked under "Imaging Mode".
Ensure that "Fluorescent" is unchecked.
Change "Exposure Time" setting for "Luminescent" to 20 s.
Set "Binning" to Medium for "Luminescent".
Set "F/stop" to 1 for "Luminescent".
Set "Emission Filter" to Open for "Luminescent".
Use the following settings for "Photograph": "Exposure Time" Auto, "Binning" Medium, and "F/stop" 8.
Adjust "Subject Height" according to imaging target.
Change "Field of View" dropdown menu from "C" to "B".
Place a microscopic slide on black construction paper in the imaging chamber.
Mix 100 µL droplet of [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2-solution with 100 µL of an aqueous solution of (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6.
Place the imaging subject on black construction paper, centered under the green light box crosshair.
Prepare nebulizer by detaching plastic spray bottle from wooden support.
Fill plastic reservoir with a solution of triethylamine in water/ethanol (1:3).
Reattach plastic spray bottle to wooden support.
Place the nebulizer inside the bioluminescence reader.
Ensure that the power switch is on and the toggle switch is off.
Check that the red LED is lit.
Position the nebulizer so that the spray flow is directed towards the area of interest on the imaging subject.
Minimize obstruction to the camera view by adjusting the position of the spray nozzle head.
Cover any potential hot spots with small, black pieces of construction paper.
Place at least 40 cm of the nebulizer remote cord inside the imaging chamber.
Ensure that the cord does not interfere with the imaging subject, the nebulizer, or the magnetic door latch.
Close the imaging system door.
Set the "Field of View" to "B" in "Living Image."
Acquire an image by initiating the imaging sequence.
Click "Acquire" in the "Acquisition Control Panel."
In a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, prepare 100 µL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution containing between 8 and 33 nmol of [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2.
Prepare an aqueous solution of (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6 in water at a concentration of 25 mM simultaneously.
Intravenously inject 100 µL of [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2 into the tail vein of healthy mice.
Euthanize the mice 10 min after injection via CO2 asphyxiation.
Make a Y-cut in the skin of the torso to remove it.
Remove the costal arch in a U-shape to expose the heart and lungs.
Cut an outlet in the right atrium.
Inject 20 mL of PBS through a 24 gauge needle into the left ventricle.
Cut longitudinally through the belly skin to expose the kidney and liver.
Create visible cuts through the organs by cutting longitudinally.
Thoroughly wash the nebulizer plastic reservoir.
Fill the nebulizer reservoir with a solution of (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6 in water at 25 mM concentration.
Rinse the nebulizer nozzle thoroughly after every use to prevent crystallization and potential damage.
Position the mouse carcass for whole abdomen imaging with the open abdomen facing the camera.
Center the organ to be imaged in the green light box crosshair for imaging.
Pin down the excised organs from the mouse for individual organ imaging and quantification.
Excise inner organs such as kidney, liver, lung, muscle, spleen, brain, and heart starting from the opened body cavity.
Cut through the hind leg skin to excise muscle tissue.
Carefully open the skull with a scalpel to excise the brain.
Prepare 10 µL of a PBS solution containing 80 nmol of [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2.
Prepare an aqueous solution of (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6 in water (25 mM).
Inject 10 µL of the Ru(bpy)3 solution subdermally into the hind paw of healthy mice.
Inject the contralateral paw with 10 µL of pure PBS as a negative control.
Sacrifice the mice via CO2 asphyxiation 15 min after injection.
Remove skin on both hind legs to expose lymph canals up to popliteal lymph nodes.
Set up acquisition as described in step 3.4.
Remove and cut popliteal lymph nodes from both hind legs.
Spray lymph node halves with oxidant on a Petri dish for quantification.
